To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the −10 regions are necessary and sufficient for sigma factor selectivity of ospE/ospf/elp promoters in B.  burgdorferii.
the −10 regions are the key determinants for the differential recognition of the promoters by σ70 or RpoS.

RpoS recognition in B. burgdorferiburgdorferi requires a specific motif in the −10 region of the promoter, and that the sequence of this motif is highly conserved in the promoters of genes that are upregulated during tick feeding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the molecular basis of gene expression in Borrelia and the role it plays in the pathogenesis of Lyme disease.
the molecular mechanisms that control the expression of genes of Borrelia spp., the causative agents of Lyme disease and relapsing fever, in response to environmental signals.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the differential expression of the ospE and ospF gene families in Borrelia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the RpoS specificity for the PospF promoter is determined by a sequence motif in the PospF −10 region, while the σ70 recognition of the PospE promoter is dependent on the −35 region and the sequence of the spacer between −35 and −10.
sigma factor selectivity in B. burgdorferis is dependent on the −10 region of the ospE and ospF promoters.
RpoS is the major transcriptional regulator for the expression of the ospF gene and the ospE/elp gene families in B. burdorferi.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
B. b. 297 is a good model for studying the Lyme disease agent.
RpoS‐mediated transcriptional control is not as robust in Borrelia as it is in E. coli.
the RpoS specificity of the ospF promoter of B. burdorferi is determined by the PospF‐10 sequence and not the PospF sequence itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the RpoS‐specific −10 region of PospF is sufficient for RpoD‐independent recognition of the ospF promoter in B. burgdorferia and that the sequence of the ospE and ospF promoters can be switched without changing the transcriptional specificity of the promoters.
the RpoS‐specific −10 element of the ospF promoter is necessary and sufficient to confer RpoS specificity in Borrelia.
the −10 region of a Borrelia burgdoferi promoter is important for RpoS selectivity.
